heroes.headline: Chip Stocks Just Booked Their Best Quarter Ever — Micron, Intel and AMD Alone Added ~$2 Trillion
heroes.one_liner: The PHLX Semiconductor Index rose ~87.8% in Q2 2026 — its biggest quarterly gain since 1994 — on an AI-driven memory and processor boom.
heroes.story: The Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor Index (SOX) rose about 87.8% in the three months ended June 30, 2026 — the biggest quarterly gain in records going back to 1994, exceeding even the dot-com era, per CNBC and Axios. The rally added roughly $2 trillion in combined market value to Micron, Intel and AMD in the quarter alone. Micron stock jumped more than 240%, Intel about 216% and AMD roughly 186%, driven by AI demand for memory chips (DRAM, NAND, HBM) that have relatively fixed near-term supply. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) rose about 71%, its best quarter since it began trading in 2000. The move came despite a violent early-June selloff, underscoring how volatile the sector has become.
heroes.founding_story: The SOX index was launched by the Philadelphia Stock Exchange in 1993-94 to track U.S.-listed semiconductor companies; it is now maintained by Nasdaq. It has become the benchmark investors watch to gauge the health of the chip cycle, and Q2 2026 was its strongest quarter in that ~30-year history.
heroes.who_should_use: Anyone tracking the AI trade, index and ETF investors with tech exposure, and traders watching sector momentum. The SOX and SMH are the go-to gauges for whether the chip cycle is expanding or rolling over.
heroes.who_should_buy: Investors who believe AI infrastructure spending keeps compounding might consider broad chip exposure (an ETF like SMH or SOXX) rather than single names. The obvious risk: after an ~88% quarter, a lot of optimism is already priced in, valuations are stretched, and the sector has shown it can drop 10% in a day. This is a momentum-heavy, high-volatility area — not a recommendation to buy.
heroes.free_alternatives: Track the index for free via Nasdaq's SOX overview page and Yahoo Finance/Google Finance sector pages. Free ETF research (holdings, expense ratios) is available on the VanEck (SMH) and iShares (SOXX) fund pages and on Morningstar's free tier.
heroes.verdict: WATCH — the AI chip boom is real and the earnings back it up, but an ~88% quarter is priced for perfection; the hype is running well ahead of any single day's fundamentals.

heroes.headline: The June 2026 Chip Scare: Broadcom's AI Guidance Miss Sparked a Trillion-Dollar Sector Selloff
heroes.one_liner: Broadcom fell ~12.6% after refusing to raise its 2026 AI-chip forecast; the chip index cratered ~10% on June 5 — its worst day since March 2020.
heroes.story: Broadcom reported fiscal Q2 2026 revenue of $22.19 billion (just under the ~$22.27B consensus) with adjusted EPS of $2.44, beating estimates, and said AI revenue more than doubled year over year to $10.8 billion, per CNBC. But the stock fell about 12.6% (closing near $418.91) — its worst session in over a year — because CEO Hock Tan declined to raise the full-year 2026 AI semiconductor forecast and guided current-quarter AI revenue to about $16 billion, below some hopes. In a market conditioned to expect ever-rising guidance, holding the line was read as a warning that AI-chip growth could be plateauing. The disappointment rippled across the sector, dragging Nvidia, AMD and Intel lower and helping trigger a broad chip selloff in early-to-mid June that reportedly erased on the order of $1 trillion-plus in sector value at its worst. It proved short-lived — the sector went on to its best quarter ever.
heroes.founding_story: Broadcom traces its roots to AT&T/Bell Labs' semiconductor unit, later HP and Agilent's chip business (Avago Technologies), which acquired the original Broadcom Corp. in 2016 and took its name. Under CEO Hock Tan it became a custom-silicon powerhouse; Tan disclosed six core custom-chip customers including Google, Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic.
heroes.who_should_use: AI-trade investors, anyone holding chip or Big Tech ETFs, and traders who need to understand how a single guidance print can move the whole sector. It is a case study in expectations vs. reality.
heroes.who_should_buy: Bargain-hunters who think the AI capex cycle is intact might view AVGO dips as entries, given its custom-chip customer roster. But the episode is a real risk flag: when a leader stops raising guidance, it can signal the cycle is maturing, and Broadcom trades at a rich multiple. Balance the growth story against concentration in a handful of hyperscaler customers. Not advice.
heroes.free_alternatives: Read Broadcom's official earnings release and 8-K on its investor site for free rather than relying on secondary summaries. Free price/quote data via Yahoo Finance and Google Finance; free sector context via Nasdaq's SOX page.
heroes.verdict: WATCH — the fundamentals (AI revenue +143%) were strong; the selloff was a hype-reset over guidance, not a broken business. A reminder that sentiment, not just numbers, drives these stocks.

heroes.headline: Nvidia Posts Record $81.6B Quarter — Data Center Nearly Doubles — Yet the Stock Slipped
heroes.one_liner: Nvidia's Q1 FY2027 revenue hit $81.6B (+85% YoY) with data center at $75.2B (+92%), and it hiked its dividend — but shares fell on the print.
heroes.story: For fiscal 2026 (ended January 2026), NVIDIA reported record revenue of $215.9 billion, up 65% year over year, per its official release. In Q1 fiscal 2027 (reported May 20, 2026), revenue reached a record $81.6 billion, up 85% year over year, with Data Center revenue of $75.2 billion up 92%, and GAAP net income of $58.3 billion, per CNBC and NVIDIA. On May 18, 2026 the board raised the quarterly dividend from $0.01 to $0.25 per share and added $80 billion to buybacks. Notably, NVIDIA booked no Data Center Hopper shipments to China in the quarter (versus $4.6 billion a year earlier) due to export restrictions, and guided Q2 revenue to about $91.0 billion with no assumed China data-center compute. Despite the blowout, the stock slid after the report as expectations were sky-high.
heroes.founding_story: NVIDIA was founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem — reportedly sketched out at a Denny's in San Jose. It pioneered the GPU in 1999, pivoted those chips into AI/accelerated computing, and by 2026 sits at the center of the AI infrastructure build-out, at times carrying a market value above $4-5 trillion.
heroes.who_should_use: Every AI investor and index holder — NVIDIA is the single largest S&P 500 component (~7.9% weight in mid-2026), so its results move the whole market. Anyone with an S&P 500 fund already owns a big slice of it.
heroes.who_should_buy: Believers in sustained AI infrastructure demand might consider NVDA, which trades at a lower forward P/E (~20x) than the chip sector average (~26.8x) despite faster growth. Risks are real: customer concentration among a few hyperscalers building their own chips (Google, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon), China export limits, and 'peak AI' fears. This is context, not a buy call.
heroes.free_alternatives: Read NVIDIA's quarterly results and CFO commentary free on investor.nvidia.com. For diversified exposure without a single-stock bet, research low-cost S&P 500 or Nasdaq-100 index funds (which hold NVDA) on the fund providers' free pages.
heroes.verdict: USE — the AI demand is unambiguously real and the numbers are extraordinary; the 'sell the news' drops show how much perfection is already baked in. Substance over hype here.

heroes.headline: The AI King Is Lagging Its Own Kingdom: Nvidia Badly Trailed the Chip Sector in 2026
heroes.one_liner: Nvidia rose ~11% in 2026 while the PHLX Semiconductor Index surged ~79-88% — an unusual gap as money rotated into memory and foundry names.
heroes.story: In a year when the PHLX Semiconductor Index rallied roughly 79-88%, Nvidia stock advanced only about 11%, a striking divergence for the company that defined the AI trade, per The Motley Fool and CNBC. The gap reflects a rotation: investors piled into memory makers (Micron up 240%+ in Q2), foundry turnaround bets (Intel up 216%) and AMD (up 186%), while worrying that Nvidia's biggest customers — Microsoft and Meta among them — are building in-house chips to cut dependence. Nvidia's forward P/E fell to about 20x, below the sector's ~26.8x average, which bulls read as cheap and bears read as skepticism about durability. The debate heading into the second half: does Nvidia catch up, or has leadership permanently broadened across the sector?
heroes.founding_story: Nvidia's dominance was built on CUDA, the software layer it launched in 2006 that locked developers into its GPUs — the moat now under question as rivals and customers design custom AI silicon. The 2026 underperformance is the first sustained test of whether that moat still commands a premium.
heroes.who_should_use: Anyone who assumes 'AI trade' equals 'buy Nvidia' — 2026 shows the sector can boom while the leader lags. Useful for investors thinking about concentration risk and rotation within a theme.
heroes.who_should_buy: Contrarians may see a relatively cheap megacap growing 85%+ with a discounted multiple. Others may prefer the diversified sector (via an ETF) that has been outrunning it. The core risk is structural: custom silicon from hyperscalers and 'peak AI capex' fears could keep a lid on the multiple. Presented as analysis, not advice.
heroes.free_alternatives: Compare NVDA vs. the SOX/SMH for free on Yahoo Finance or Google Finance charts. Free analyst summaries and valuation snapshots are on Motley Fool's free articles and Morningstar's free tier.
heroes.verdict: WATCH — a rare and instructive divergence; the hype ('just buy Nvidia') collided with a reality where memory and foundry names led. The setup for H2 is genuinely uncertain.

heroes.one_liner: Agility Robotics (maker of Digit) plans a Nasdaq listing via Churchill Capital XI at ~$2.5B — the first pure-play U.S.-listed humanoid robot company.
heroes.story: Agility Robotics, the Oregon company behind the two-legged Digit robot, announced on June 24, 2026 that it will go public by merging with Churchill Capital Corp XI at an implied valuation of about $2.5 billion, per TechCrunch and PitchBook. The deal is expected to bring in more than $600 million in gross proceeds — roughly $420 million from Churchill XI's trust plus over $200 million from a PIPE led by existing backer Foxconn. Upon closing, the combined company is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the ticker AGLT, becoming the first pure-play humanoid-robot maker listed in the U.S. Unlike most humanoid startups, Agility says Digit is already working across nine customer facilities with more than 65,000 hours of operation and over $300 million in multi-year Digit v5 orders (subject to milestones) from a pipeline of 30-plus customers.
heroes.founding_story: Agility Robotics was spun out of Oregon State University in 2015 by robotics researchers Damion Shelton, Jonathan Hurst and Mikhail Jones, building on years of bipedal-locomotion research (the 'Cassie' and later 'Digit' robots). It opened 'RoboFab,' billed as a factory for mass-producing humanoids, ahead of this public-market debut.
heroes.who_should_use: Investors watching the humanoid-robotics and automation theme, warehouse/logistics operators evaluating labor automation, and anyone tracking how speculative AI-adjacent hardware reaches public markets.
heroes.who_should_buy: Risk-tolerant investors who want early exposure to commercial humanoids might watch AGLT once it lists — Agility's real deployments and Foxconn backing set it apart. But SPAC de-listings are historically high-risk: valuations often outrun revenue, orders here are milestone-dependent, humanoid economics are unproven at scale, and competition (Tesla Optimus, Figure) is fierce. Treat as speculative; this is not a recommendation.
heroes.free_alternatives: You cannot buy shares until the merger closes; until then, read the deal materials free via TechCrunch and The Robot Report. For diversified robotics/automation exposure, research robotics-and-AI ETFs (e.g., BOTZ, ROBO) on the fund providers' free pages instead of a single pre-revenue-scale name.
heroes.verdict: WATCH — genuinely notable as the first U.S. humanoid pure-play with real deployments, but a SPAC at $2.5B is a hype-forward vehicle; let the fundamentals prove out post-listing.

heroes.headline: OpenClaw becomes the most-starred repo in GitHub history and lands native iOS and Android apps
heroes.one_liner: The free, self-hosted personal AI agent 'Molty' crossed ~381k stars and just shipped mobile apps that pair your phone to your own assistant.
heroes.story: OpenClaw is a free, open-source, self-hostable personal AI assistant you run on your own devices; it plugs into messaging channels you already use (WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, iMessage, Slack, Signal and more) and executes tasks through a modular 'Skills' system for browser automation, API calls and file operations. As of July 1, 2026 the GitHub repo showed roughly 381,000 stars, making it by multiple accounts the most-starred software repository in GitHub history and one of the fastest-growing ever. On June 30, 2026, TechCrunch reported OpenClaw finally launched native iOS and Android apps that pair a phone to the user's 'OpenClaw Gateway,' granting the agent access to camera, screen, location, photos, contacts and calendar. A credibility asterisk: TechCrunch and others reported that the earlier viral 'MoltBook' agent-society moment was partly humans impersonating AI agents, so some of the hype was theater rather than autonomous behavior.
heroes.founding_story: OpenClaw was created by Austrian developer Peter Steinberger, founder and former CEO of PSPDFKit, who released the project in November 2025 after a hiatus and a move into AI 'vibe coding.' It was renamed twice (Clawdbot, then Moltbot, then OpenClaw) partly after a trademark complaint. In February 2026, Reuters and Forbes reported Steinberger joined OpenAI (turning down a Meta offer) and that the open-source project was moved into an independent OpenClaw Foundation that OpenAI supports.
heroes.who_should_use: Tinkerers and privacy-minded power users who want a personal AI agent that runs on their own hardware and acts through the chat apps they already use.
heroes.who_should_buy: It's free and open source (MIT-licensed per coverage) - there's nothing to buy. Your only real costs are optional: a machine or small server to self-host it and pay-as-you-go API fees for whatever LLM you point it at.
heroes.free_alternatives: OpenClaw itself is the free/open alternative to paid personal-assistant and 'agentic' products; closest comparisons are commercial assistants and agent platforms you'd otherwise pay for, plus self-hosted rivals like the open-source Pi coding-agent SDK it builds on.
heroes.verdict: WATCH - Genuinely the biggest open-source story of 2026 and free to run, but granting a self-hosted agent your camera, contacts and screen is a real security bet; pilot it in a sandbox before you trust it with your life.

heroes.headline: OpenCode races past 180k stars as the leading open-source, model-agnostic terminal coding agent
heroes.one_liner: A free CLI coding agent that works with 75+ model providers (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Ollama) hit ~181k stars and shipped v1.17.13 on July 1.
heroes.story: OpenCode is a free, open-source (MIT), terminal-native AI coding agent that is deliberately model-agnostic: it works with 75+ providers including Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini and locally-run Ollama models, so you're not locked to one vendor. As of July 1, 2026 the GitHub repo showed roughly 181,000 stars and 22.4k forks, with a very fast release cadence (830 releases; v1.17.13 shipped July 1, 2026) and a growing desktop app in beta. It ships two built-in agents you can switch between - a full-access 'build' agent and a read-only 'plan' agent - plus a 'general' subagent for multi-step searches. The repo now lives under the 'anomalyco' organization (the original 'sst/opencode' URL redirects there), reflecting a move to a dedicated company behind the project. Coverage through 2026 has repeatedly ranked it the top open-source CLI coding agent, with reports that its growth is outpacing closed rivals like Cursor.
heroes.founding_story: OpenCode grew out of the SST (Serverless Stack) developer-tools ecosystem and was built as an open, editor-agnostic alternative to closed AI coding tools, letting developers bring their own model API keys instead of paying a single vendor. The project has since been consolidated under the 'anomalyco' GitHub organization as its backing company, while keeping the code MIT-licensed and community-driven.
heroes.who_should_use: Developers who want an AI pair-programmer in the terminal but insist on choosing their own model - or running local models - rather than being tied to one proprietary IDE.
heroes.who_should_buy: The tool is free and open source; you only pay for the model tokens you consume (e.g. Claude or GPT API usage), or nothing at all if you point it at a local model via Ollama.
heroes.free_alternatives: OpenCode is the free/open alternative to paid coding assistants like Cursor and GitHub Copilot; other free options include Aider, Cline and the Pi coding agent.
heroes.verdict: USE - If you want a serious AI coding agent that respects model choice and your budget, it's free, actively maintained, and a legitimate rival to paid IDEs - just supply your own API key or a local model.

heroes.headline: Ollama tops 175k stars and rolls out a native desktop app for running LLMs locally
heroes.one_liner: The simplest way to run models like DeepSeek, Qwen, Gemma and gpt-oss on your own machine added a Mac and Windows app and faster Apple Silicon inference.
heroes.story: Ollama is a free, open-source tool that lets you download and run large language models locally on macOS, Windows and Linux, packaging each model behind a simple command and a local API so no data leaves your machine. As of July 1, 2026 the GitHub repo showed roughly 175,000 stars, and the project's tagline advertises out-of-the-box support for current open models including DeepSeek, Qwen, Gemma and OpenAI's gpt-oss. In 2026 Ollama shipped a native desktop app for macOS and Windows (a friendlier front end than the CLI) and pushed frequent June releases that upgraded its Apple Silicon MLX engine, broadened GGUF hardware support and refreshed its llama.cpp backend. Note some specifics reported by third-party release trackers - exact version numbers and 'new models added this month' - are lower-confidence than the core facts.
heroes.founding_story: Ollama is built by Ollama Inc., a Palo Alto startup founded in 2023 by Jeffrey Morgan (ex-Docker) and Michael Chiang and backed via Y Combinator. Their goal was to make running local LLMs as easy as installing a single binary, abstracting away model weights, quantization and GPU setup so anyone could run open models offline.
heroes.who_should_use: Developers, privacy-conscious users and anyone who wants to run open-weight models offline or wire a local model into other tools without cloud costs.
heroes.who_should_buy: It's free and open source - nothing to buy. The only cost is your own hardware; bigger models want a capable GPU or Apple Silicon with enough RAM.
heroes.free_alternatives: Ollama is itself the free alternative to paid cloud LLM APIs; comparable free/open runners include llama.cpp (its underlying engine), LM Studio (free desktop app) and Jan.
heroes.verdict: USE - The default, no-cost way to run capable AI models on your own machine; pair it with Open WebUI or OpenCode and you have a private stack that replaces paid subscriptions for many tasks.

heroes.headline: Pi, a radically minimal coding agent, explodes from ~14k to ~58k stars and moves to Armin Ronacher's Earendil
heroes.one_liner: A tiny, hackable terminal coding agent with just four tools and a sub-1,000-token prompt became 2026's fastest-rising net-new dev tool.
heroes.story: Pi is a free, open-source (MIT) AI agent toolkit whose headline piece is a radically minimal terminal coding agent: it exposes only four tools (read, write, edit, bash) and a system prompt under roughly 1,000 tokens, and is explicitly 'built to be forked and rewired' rather than to dictate a workflow. It went viral in 2026 as the fastest-rising net-new coding agent, growing from about 14k stars in February to roughly 58k when it moved to the Earendil organization in May, and around 61k reported in June. Beyond the CLI it ships a unified LLM API and agent-loop SDK, and its author notes they 'use Pi to build Pi.' The repository moved from 'badlogic/pi-mono' to 'earendil-works/pi,' so confirm the current URL; some star figures come from blog write-ups rather than a live GitHub read.
heroes.founding_story: Pi was created by Mario Zechner (known as 'badlogic,' creator of the libGDX game framework), who built it as a deliberately tiny, transparent alternative to heavyweight AI coding tools. In April 2026 Zechner joined Earendil - a venture-backed public-benefit corporation co-founded by Armin Ronacher (creator of Flask and Jinja2) - and brought Pi with him; the repo moved to earendil-works/pi while staying MIT-licensed, and OpenClaw uses Pi's SDK under the hood.
heroes.who_should_use: Developers and tinkerers who want a coding agent small enough to actually read, understand and modify - a base to build their own agent on rather than a black box.
heroes.who_should_buy: Free and open source; you only pay for whatever model API you plug into it (or nothing with a local model).
heroes.free_alternatives: Pi is the minimalist free alternative to paid coding assistants like Cursor and Copilot; other free/open peers include OpenCode, Aider and Cline.
heroes.verdict: USE - If you like understanding your tools, Pi is a delight: free, hackable and legitimately influential (it underpins OpenClaw). Casual users wanting turnkey polish may prefer OpenCode.

heroes.headline: ComfyUI hits a $500M valuation as the open-source hub for controllable AI image and video
heroes.one_liner: The free node-based tool for Stable Diffusion, Flux and open video models raised $30M and keeps adding WAN and HunyuanVideo workflows.
heroes.story: ComfyUI is a free, open-source, node/graph-based interface and backend for building modular generative-AI workflows - chaining models, prompts and steps visually instead of writing code - and it has become the power-user hub for open image and video generation (Stable Diffusion, Flux, Hunyuan and more). Star counts put it well into the 110k-119k range by mid-2026 (Wikipedia recorded 89.2k in September 2025). In April 2026, TechCrunch reported ComfyUI's company, Comfy Org, raised $30M at a roughly $500M valuation led by Craft Ventures, as creators sought more control over AI-generated media. The project actively ships a desktop app and has added support for newer open video models such as WAN 2.1 and HunyuanVideo (including image-to-video), extending it from images into video pipelines.
heroes.founding_story: ComfyUI was created by the pseudonymous developer 'comfyanonymous,' with its first release in January 2023, aiming to improve on existing Stable Diffusion UIs with a flexible node-based design. comfyanonymous worked at Stability AI until mid-2024; after leaving, the core developers formed the Comfy Org organization (June 2024) to steward the project and build a company around it, later raising venture funding.
heroes.who_should_use: Artists, technical creators and researchers who want fine-grained, reproducible control over AI image and video generation and are willing to learn a node-based workflow.
heroes.who_should_buy: The software is free and open source; costs are optional - your own GPU (or a rented cloud GPU) to run heavier image and video models locally.
heroes.free_alternatives: ComfyUI is the free/open alternative to paid generative tools like Midjourney, DALL-E and Runway; other free options include Automatic1111 and Fooocus for simpler image generation.
heroes.verdict: USE - If you want maximum control over open image and video models without subscription fees, ComfyUI is the standard - just budget a capable GPU and a learning curve; casual users may prefer simpler paid apps.

all_news.verdict: WATCH - The most important eVTOL story of the month: it fixes Joby's manufacturing risk, but there's still no certified aircraft or paying passenger, so it's a strong watch, not a buy.

all_news.headline: Joby's first FAA-conforming air taxi enters final certification as Dubai launch nears
all_news.one_liner: Aircraft N547JX is flying Stage 5 (the last FAA phase) while Joby targets its first commercial passenger service in Dubai in 2026.
all_news.verdict: WATCH - Genuinely close to the finish line and Dubai is the most credible near-term launch, but 'flying Stage 5' is not 'certified,' so watch for the FAA sign-off before believing the timeline.

all_news.headline: Archer's Midnight pushes toward first passengers in Abu Dhabi and US pilot cities
all_news.one_liner: First eVTOL to clear 100% of FAA 'Means of Compliance,' Archer is testing Midnight in the UAE and lining up US operations under the federal eIPP.
all_news.source_name: Archer Aviation / Gulf News / 24/7 Wall St
all_news.verdict: WATCH - Archer is arguably tied with Joby on paper and leads on Means of Compliance, but until it shows a public piloted transition flight and a real passenger, treat the hype with caution.

all_news.headline: UK's Vertical Aerospace flies its final VX4 prototype ahead of Farnborough
all_news.one_liner: Vertical's third and last full-scale prototype made its maiden piloted flight on June 5, 2026, doubling flight-test capacity before Critical Design Review.
all_news.source_name: Business Wire (Vertical Aerospace) / FlightGlobal / Aviation Week
all_news.verdict: WATCH - Real, verifiable flight-test progress and a survivor in a brutal European market, but thin finances and a still-distant CDR make it a watch, and only a speculative one for investors.

all_news.headline: Beta, Surf Air and Hawaiian Airlines start flying electric aircraft across Hawaii
all_news.one_liner: A 6-to-8-week trial of Beta's Alia CX300 electric plane began June 25, 2026, testing interisland electric flight in Hawaii.
all_news.verdict: USE - This is the rare eVTOL-adjacent story where real electric aircraft are flying real missions now; if you're in Hawaii, watch for the resulting commercial service, and investors get a comparatively de-risked name to track.

all_news.headline: US Transportation Secretary becomes first to fly in an eVTOL
all_news.one_liner: Sean Duffy flew Beta's Alia in Vermont on May 29, 2026, as DOT and the FAA unveiled a 26-state eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP).
all_news.source_name: US Department of Transportation / FLYING Magazine

all_news.headline: FAA to build an air-taxi research and test range in Oklahoma City
all_news.one_liner: The agency's Vertical Takeoff and Landing Procedures and Analysis Range (V-PAR) could come online as soon as next summer.

all_news.headline: Joby ramps up Dayton, Ohio production as it nears FAA approval
all_news.one_liner: Joby is expanding manufacturing at its Dayton site, positioning it as a core hub for eVTOL fleet production ahead of certification.

all_news.headline: Vertical Aerospace lines up more Valo suppliers (Astronics, Hyundai WIA)
all_news.one_liner: Vertical named Astronics for low-voltage power distribution and Hyundai WIA for landing gear, filling out its production supply chain.

all_news.headline: Analysts split on air-taxi stocks as certification nears
all_news.one_liner: With Joby and Archer approaching FAA sign-off, commentators debate whether the shares are overhyped or still deeply undervalued.

all_news.headline: eVTOL lawsuits and infighting cloud the US launch push
all_news.one_liner: CNBC reports court battles and disputes could complicate the industry's long-hyped US commercial breakthrough even as testing accelerates.

all_news.headline: Anduril and General Atomics Win Air Force Contracts to Build America's First AI Fighter-Drone Wingmen
all_news.one_liner: The Air Force greenlit production of the FQ-44 (Anduril) and FQ-42 (General Atomics) — the first mass-produced autonomous AI jet wingmen.
all_news.verdict: WATCH — a genuine landmark in autonomous air combat, but there is nothing to buy; ignore anyone selling you 'Anduril shares.'

all_news.headline: DJI Launches O4 Ground Station to Push Enterprise Drones Up to 40 km Past Dead Zones
all_news.one_liner: A rugged 12-antenna relay that extends DJI Dock 3 and Matrice 400 transmission to 30-40 km for 24/7 autonomous inspection and search-and-rescue.
all_news.verdict: USE / BUY (for existing DJI fleets) — a real, well-specced range upgrade; US buyers should confirm import status first.

all_news.headline: Antigravity A1, the World's First 8K 360 Drone, Goes on Sale Worldwide
all_news.one_liner: Insta360's new drone brand ships a sub-250g flyer with a built-in 8K 360 camera, FPV goggles, and 'look anywhere while flying anywhere' FreeMotion controls.
all_news.verdict: BUY (for 360 creators) — genuinely first-of-its-kind and purchasable; overkill if you just want a normal camera drone.

all_news.headline: Ukraine Unveils 'Sea Trident ST-1000,' a 10-Ton Underwater Attack Drone, at Eurosatory 2026
all_news.one_liner: Global Mark's first extra-large underwater drone carries a 1,000 kg payload up to ~3,200 km and fits inside a standard shipping container.
all_news.verdict: WATCH — a striking signal of where undersea warfare is heading, but nothing to buy or invest in.

all_news.headline: VisionWave Debuts Combat-Ready TALON and D-FLY Autonomous Drones at Eurosatory 2026
all_news.one_liner: Nasdaq-listed VisionWave unveiled a jamming-resistant ISR drone (TALON) and an autonomous counter-drone interceptor (D-FLY) under its STRATUM autonomy stack.
all_news.verdict: WATCH — legitimately unveiled and interesting, but a speculative small-cap with vendor-stated specs; not a buy for consumers.

all_news.headline: Ondas Launches LADOS Counter-Drone Command-and-Control Layer at Eurosatory 2026
all_news.one_liner: Ondas (Nasdaq: ONDS) unveiled LADOS, a hardware-agnostic C2 'system of systems' linking any sensor, drone, and effector; first European deliveries hinted for Q3 2026.

all_news.headline: Skydio CEO Adam Bry Argues Against 'Red Lines' on Drone Autonomy
all_news.one_liner: On the June 15, 2026 Decoder podcast, Bry said Silicon Valley shouldn't restrict autonomous-drone development and that wider use will make communities safer.

all_news.headline: Skydio X10 Drone-First-Responder Program Used to Arrest Fleeing Suspect in Colorado
all_news.one_liner: Arvada, CO police used a Skydio X10 DFR deployment on June 17, 2026 to track and arrest a shoplifting suspect who fled a Target on foot.

all_news.headline: DJI Stays on FCC Covered List; Firmware/Security Updates Extended to 2029
all_news.one_liner: New DJI models still can't get US import authorization, but the FCC extended security-update support to Jan 1, 2029 (DA-26-454) — existing drones keep flying.

all_news.headline: Marine Corps to Award Sole-Source Counter-Drone Contract to Anduril
all_news.one_liner: The USMC plans a sole-source deal for Anduril's Pulsar-Lite C-sUAS electronic-warfare packages to protect Amphibious Combat Vehicles.

all_news.headline: DEA Eyes Skydio and Parrot Drones for Its Growing Arsenal
all_news.one_liner: The Drug Enforcement Administration is looking to add Skydio R10 hardware/software bundles and Parrot drones, favoring US and allied (non-DJI) makers.

all_news.headline: Meta drops the Ray-Ban logo: new in-house 'Meta Glasses' start at $299 and ship now
all_news.one_liner: Meta's first self-designed AI smart glasses undercut Ray-Ban Meta at $299, run the new Muse Spark model, and are on sale today.
all_news.verdict: BUY - the best-value entry into Meta's mature smart-glasses ecosystem, as long as you do not need an in-lens display.

all_news.headline: Valve's new Steam Machine is real: $1,049, ships June 30 - but pre-orders were a lottery that closed June 25
all_news.one_liner: Valve's redesigned SteamOS living-room PC starts at $1,049 and began shipping June 30, sold via a randomized reservation queue.
all_news.verdict: WATCH - a genuinely appealing SteamOS console, but the lottery-only sales and RAM-driven $1,049 price mean you should wait for reviews and open stock before committing.

all_news.headline: Samsung's Galaxy XR headset lands in the UK: pre-orders open at GBP 1,699, ships July 8
all_news.one_liner: Samsung's Android XR headset (US$1,799) opens UK pre-orders at GBP 1,699 on June 17, shipping July 8 - a cheaper Vision Pro rival.
all_news.verdict: WATCH - impressive hardware and far cheaper than Vision Pro, but a young app ecosystem means only committed early adopters should buy now.

all_news.headline: Nvidia RTX Spark: a wave of AI-first Windows laptops and mini PCs is locked in for fall 2026
all_news.one_liner: Nvidia's RTX Spark superchip (Arm CPU + Blackwell GPU, up to 128GB) will power Windows 'agentic AI' PCs from Dell, HP, Lenovo, ASUS and Surface this fall.
all_news.verdict: WATCH - a promising leap for on-device AI PCs, but with fall availability and no confirmed prices, there is nothing to buy in July 2026.

all_news.headline: Samsung sets Galaxy Unpacked for July 22: Z Fold 8, Z Fold 8 Ultra, Z Flip 8 and Galaxy Glasses incoming
all_news.one_liner: Samsung's next Unpacked is heavily signaled for July 22 in London, with pre-orders expected to open the same day for its 2026 foldables.
all_news.verdict: WATCH - the launch is essentially here, so hold off on any Samsung foldable purchase until the July 22 Unpacked pricing is official.

all_news.headline: OnePlus 15R ships globally at $699 - first phone with Snapdragon 8 Gen 5, but the camera got cut back
all_news.one_liner: OnePlus's mid-range 15R (7,400 mAh battery, 165Hz gaming display) beat its own flagship to Snapdragon 8 Gen 5, though reviewers flag the dropped telephoto and price hike.

all_news.headline: DJI Osmo Pocket 4 Pro rolls out internationally (June 29) with a 1-inch sensor and 3x zoom - but not officially in the US
all_news.one_liner: DJI's first 'Pro' pocket vlogging camera adds a 1-inch sensor, telephoto zoom and D-Log2, landing in Asia/Europe around $650-$730 with no US FCC certification.

all_news.headline: Nothing confirms Ear (3a) budget earbuds for July 7, alongside the Phone (4b)
all_news.one_liner: Nothing officially set a July 7 launch for its ~$99 Ear (3a) earbuds and Phone (4b), with pre-registration open now.

all_news.headline: Meta also teases its own $299-and-up own-brand styles beyond Ray-Ban, as smart-glasses shipments jump 167%
all_news.one_liner: IDC-style figures cited at launch show smart-glasses shipments up 167% year over year in Q1 2026, with Meta holding roughly 69% of the market.

all_news.headline: Microsoft teases Surface Laptop Ultra - its 'most powerful Surface ever' - with Nvidia RTX Spark silicon
all_news.one_liner: Microsoft's upcoming Surface Laptop Ultra pairs a 15-inch mini-LED display and up to 128GB RAM with Nvidia's RTX Spark chip, due this fall at a premium price.

all_news.headline: Garmin's screen-free CIRQA smart band emerges as a subscription-free Whoop rival for 2026
all_news.one_liner: Garmin's rumored CIRQA 24/7 band (ECG, HRV, ~10-14 day battery) targets Whoop without a monthly fee, expected around mid-2026.

all_news.headline: Chip Stocks Just Booked Their Best Quarter Ever — Micron, Intel and AMD Alone Added ~$2 Trillion
all_news.one_liner: The PHLX Semiconductor Index rose ~87.8% in Q2 2026 — its biggest quarterly gain since 1994 — on an AI-driven memory and processor boom.
all_news.verdict: WATCH — the AI chip boom is real and the earnings back it up, but an ~88% quarter is priced for perfection; the hype is running well ahead of any single day's fundamentals.

all_news.headline: The June 2026 Chip Scare: Broadcom's AI Guidance Miss Sparked a Trillion-Dollar Sector Selloff
all_news.one_liner: Broadcom fell ~12.6% after refusing to raise its 2026 AI-chip forecast; the chip index cratered ~10% on June 5 — its worst day since March 2020.
all_news.verdict: WATCH — the fundamentals (AI revenue +143%) were strong; the selloff was a hype-reset over guidance, not a broken business. A reminder that sentiment, not just numbers, drives these stocks.

all_news.headline: Nvidia Posts Record $81.6B Quarter — Data Center Nearly Doubles — Yet the Stock Slipped
all_news.one_liner: Nvidia's Q1 FY2027 revenue hit $81.6B (+85% YoY) with data center at $75.2B (+92%), and it hiked its dividend — but shares fell on the print.
all_news.verdict: USE — the AI demand is unambiguously real and the numbers are extraordinary; the 'sell the news' drops show how much perfection is already baked in. Substance over hype here.

all_news.headline: The AI King Is Lagging Its Own Kingdom: Nvidia Badly Trailed the Chip Sector in 2026
all_news.one_liner: Nvidia rose ~11% in 2026 while the PHLX Semiconductor Index surged ~79-88% — an unusual gap as money rotated into memory and foundry names.
all_news.verdict: WATCH — a rare and instructive divergence; the hype ('just buy Nvidia') collided with a reality where memory and foundry names led. The setup for H2 is genuinely uncertain.

all_news.headline: Humanoids Hit Wall Street: Agility Robotics to Go Public in a $2.5B SPAC Deal
all_news.one_liner: Agility Robotics (maker of Digit) plans a Nasdaq listing via Churchill Capital XI at ~$2.5B — the first pure-play U.S.-listed humanoid robot company.
all_news.verdict: WATCH — genuinely notable as the first U.S. humanoid pure-play with real deployments, but a SPAC at $2.5B is a hype-forward vehicle; let the fundamentals prove out post-listing.

all_news.headline: Micron Reports Its Biggest Quarter Ever on AI Memory Demand
all_news.one_liner: Micron posted record fiscal-Q3 2026 revenue of ~$41.5B (up ~346% YoY) with an ~84.6% gross margin and guided Q4 to about $50B, driven by HBM.

all_news.headline: Intel Stock Surges on Reported ~3 Million-Unit Google TPU Foundry Order
all_news.one_liner: Intel jumped ~10-13% on June 8 after reports Google will have Intel manufacture 3M+ TPUs (delivery ~2028); note: no company filing yet confirmed it.

all_news.headline: Qualcomm Sharpens Data-Center Push at June 24 Investor Day
all_news.one_liner: Qualcomm targets $15B+ in data-center revenue by FY2029 and raised its FY2029 non-handset target to $40B; shares had round-tripped to ~$226 in June.

all_news.headline: Broadcom's AI Revenue Soared 143% — and the Stock Still Fell
all_news.one_liner: The paradox behind the June scare: Broadcom's AI chip revenue jumped ~143% YoY, but investors punished it for not raising full-year AI guidance.

all_news.headline: AI Chip Rally Added Roughly $2 Trillion to Micron, Intel and AMD in Q2
all_news.one_liner: CNBC tallied the record quarter: the combined market value of Micron, Intel and AMD rose about $2 trillion in the three months ended June 30, 2026.

all_news.headline: Semiconductors Post Best Quarter Since 1994, Rivaling Dot-Com Mania
all_news.one_liner: Axios: the PHLX Semiconductor Index rose ~87.8% in Q2 2026, the biggest quarterly gain in records back to 1994, powered almost entirely by the AI memory squeeze.

all_news.headline: OpenClaw becomes the most-starred repo in GitHub history and lands native iOS and Android apps
all_news.one_liner: The free, self-hosted personal AI agent 'Molty' crossed ~381k stars and just shipped mobile apps that pair your phone to your own assistant.
all_news.verdict: WATCH - Genuinely the biggest open-source story of 2026 and free to run, but granting a self-hosted agent your camera, contacts and screen is a real security bet; pilot it in a sandbox before you trust it with your life.

all_news.headline: OpenCode races past 180k stars as the leading open-source, model-agnostic terminal coding agent
all_news.one_liner: A free CLI coding agent that works with 75+ model providers (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Ollama) hit ~181k stars and shipped v1.17.13 on July 1.
all_news.verdict: USE - If you want a serious AI coding agent that respects model choice and your budget, it's free, actively maintained, and a legitimate rival to paid IDEs - just supply your own API key or a local model.

all_news.headline: Ollama tops 175k stars and rolls out a native desktop app for running LLMs locally
all_news.one_liner: The simplest way to run models like DeepSeek, Qwen, Gemma and gpt-oss on your own machine added a Mac and Windows app and faster Apple Silicon inference.
all_news.verdict: USE - The default, no-cost way to run capable AI models on your own machine; pair it with Open WebUI or OpenCode and you have a private stack that replaces paid subscriptions for many tasks.

all_news.headline: Pi, a radically minimal coding agent, explodes from ~14k to ~58k stars and moves to Armin Ronacher's Earendil
all_news.one_liner: A tiny, hackable terminal coding agent with just four tools and a sub-1,000-token prompt became 2026's fastest-rising net-new dev tool.
all_news.verdict: USE - If you like understanding your tools, Pi is a delight: free, hackable and legitimately influential (it underpins OpenClaw). Casual users wanting turnkey polish may prefer OpenCode.

all_news.headline: ComfyUI hits a $500M valuation as the open-source hub for controllable AI image and video
all_news.one_liner: The free node-based tool for Stable Diffusion, Flux and open video models raised $30M and keeps adding WAN and HunyuanVideo workflows.
all_news.verdict: USE - If you want maximum control over open image and video models without subscription fees, ComfyUI is the standard - just budget a capable GPU and a learning curve; casual users may prefer simpler paid apps.

all_news.headline: Andrej Karpathy's nanochat crosses 55k stars as the 'ChatGPT you can train for ~$100'
all_news.one_liner: The minimal full-stack LLM training/inference codebase stayed active into 2026, with speedrun entries training a GPT-2-grade model in under two hours.

all_news.headline: Ollama's llama.cpp engine keeps climbing toward ~118k stars
all_news.one_liner: llama.cpp, the C/C++ project that powers much of local LLM inference (now under the ggml-org org), remains the reference engine for running models on modest hardware.

all_news.headline: Dify passes ~142k stars as an open-source platform for building LLM and agent apps
all_news.one_liner: The visual LLM-app builder from LangGenius crossed 100k stars in 2026, though its license is Apache 2.0 with extra conditions rather than pure OSI open source.

all_news.headline: Langflow ships v1.10.0 under IBM ownership, sitting at ~150k stars
all_news.one_liner: The low-code visual builder for AI agents and RAG (MIT-licensed) released v1.10.0 on June 9, now owned by IBM via its DataStax acquisition.

all_news.headline: n8n reportedly valued at ~$5.2B with an SAP stake as AI-agent workflows surge
all_news.one_liner: The popular 'fair-code' automation tool (source-available, not OSI open source) is now used mostly for AI agents; secondary reports cite a $5.2B valuation and SAP investment.

all_news.headline: RAGFlow adds a browser agent and WhatsApp/DingTalk/WeCom channels
all_news.one_liner: The open-source RAG engine built on deep document understanding (~80k stars) shipped v0.25.4 and late-June integrations that let it navigate the web and chat apps.

all_news.headline: vLLM releases v0.22.1 as a PyTorch Foundation-hosted inference engine
all_news.one_liner: The high-throughput LLM serving engine born at UC Berkeley (PagedAttention, ~83k stars) shipped v0.22.1 on June 5 with broad multi-vendor hardware support.
